stem:
Rina studies the three pictures in the figure. Each picture is a square grid of dots: a 1-by-1 square, then a 2-by-2 square, then a 3-by-3 square.

Which claim correctly describes how to draw the next picture?

options.text: Any larger cluster of dots works, without keeping the square-grid construction from picture to picture.
Drawing the next square grid is what creates the square numbers in the first place.
The next picture is a 4-by-4 square of 16 dots, because each picture is an n-by-n square for n = 1, 2, 3, …
The next picture needs the full chapter shape-sequence table before it can be drawn.

teacher.key_rationale: The pictures encode square numbers as n-by-n grids, so the next term is the 4-by-4 grid. Dropping the grid rule breaks the encoding. Drawing does not create the sequence rule. The full table is outside this hinge.

mx_swap.reason: Mechanism-conflation CWO imports a bare generative-rule hinge already covered elsewhere; kept condition_omission, relationship_reversal, scope_error on the pictorial encoding.
